newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel cancels Monday engagements due to a cold.
newsitem.headline: Waigel cancels Monday engagements due to a cold.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel cancelled his engagements on Monday because he has caught a cold, but was due to be back in action in Bonn on Tuesday, his Christian Social Union (CSU) party said.

Waigel, under intense pressure lately to put Germany's finances into order next year to qualify for European economic and monetary union, has been bed-ridden since addressing his CSU party's annual conference last Saturday, a party spokesman said.
The 57-year-old minister had been due to speak at a symposium in Munich on the future of the European Union, and also had a speaking engagement later in the day in Bonn.
Waigel's 1997 budget will be scrutinised by parliament this week and will go to a final vote in the Bundestag lower house at the end of the week.

His tax bill, now in parliament's mediation committee, goes before the upper house, which is controlled by the opposition Social Democrats (SPD). A compromise over disputed issues, like the abolition of wealth tax, must be reached with the SPD before the measure can become law.
